class_name: 同格-堅い表現-トコロノ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1: author → mechanical attachment gate → cold review → fixes applied → gate re-run

patterns.usage_note: A stiff, overtly bookish relative-clause marker inserted between a modifying clause and the noun it modifies, where plain Japanese would simply juxtapose the two. It grew out of the 漢文訓読 use of 所 and was then pressed into service as a calque of European relative pronouns, so dictionaries describe it as belonging mostly to 翻訳調 written style; in ordinary speech it sounds affected or parodic. Because it adds little meaning, it is almost always deletable without loss of meaning, and its real work is rhythmic: it keeps a long modifying clause from crashing into its head noun in academic, legal or philosophical prose.

examples.ruby: 著者[ちょしゃ]が本書[ほんしょ]で試[こころ]みるところの分析[ぶんせき]である。
examples.english: This is the analysis which the author attempts in the present volume.

examples.ruby: 我々[われわれ]が正義[せいぎ]と呼[よ]ぶところのものは何[なに]か。
examples.english: What, then, is that which we call justice?

examples.ruby: 本論[ほんろん]では、法[ほう]が保護[ほご]するところの利益[りえき]を検討[けんとう]する。
examples.english: This paper examines the interests which the law protects.
